6. Mechanical results—and the checks that prevent acceptance

The static calculations include beam bending and torsion, joint compliance, thermal/rest-length uncertainty, foundation compliance and a conservative geometric-stiffness check.

Maximum static repair-holder force	1.688 kN	2.609 kN	1.614 kN
Maximum static repair-holder moment	285.7 Nm	375.9 Nm	286.7 Nm

The separate local rail allowance is 0.475 mm. Thus:

Accepted cantilever: 9.054 mm.
Held cantilever repair: 9.573 mm.
Worst modeled individual anchor tension: 3.101 kN.

The represented material and conservative geometric tangents remain positive. That supports the stated finite family; it does not certify fracture, arbitrary damaged connections or unknown foundations.

The current trace completes its two material repairs about 2.32 h and 1.69 h after the hidden degradation events. The admitted class therefore requires residual capacity of at least 4 kN without further degradation during a declared three-hour detection-and-repair interval.

This addresses the earlier 2 kN versus larger transfer-force mismatch for the represented class. It does not cover an advancing crack that reaches fracture before detection.

The full cut-transient certificate still fails to close

The complete algebraic mask calculation covers 10,616,832 combinations of outer-load vertices, three effective jam-stiffness points, mask pairs and connection locations. Cutting both outer interfaces restores the independent prior host/bar equilibrium in those represented cases.

Its maximum calculated energies are:

Structural release energy: 1.264 J.
Retained internal jam/counter/cage energy: 7.617 J.

But its conservative dynamic bounds reach:

Holder force: 6.369 kN.
Holder moment: 1,179 Nm.
Rotation: 25.077 mrad.
